_comment: Shipped tile providers. See docs/design/providers.md for the reasoning, the measurements and
the checklist every entry must pass. A file of this shape in the user's configuration
directory is merged over this one, so adding a provider needs no build and no release.
Templates marked 'probed' were verified by fetching a real tile on 2026-09-18 and recording
what came back. The rest are from provider documentation and are unverified because they need
bulkDownload=false means viewing only: the downloader refuses a job that would fetch more than
256 missing tiles, and nothing overrides that.
{scale} is where a provider puts @2x: a template with it offers tiles of the same ground at
512 px, and a theme without them has a template of its own without the token. Probed with a
key on 2026-10-01 for Mapy.com; the others are from their documentation.
The order is the catalog's, and it decides something: a first run fetches its world from the
first provider that is global and needs no key. That is OpenStreetMap, so it comes before Esri.
A provider's languages are in an order too: the first is its own, which a map of it is lettered
in where nothing names one – a project file without source.lang, wtf-tiles without --lang.
A provider whose terms ask for its logo with the attribution names it in logo: an SVG file in
logos/ beside this one, the provider's own as published. The credit is printed with it.

themes.note: Probed: image/jpeg. World only to z13; Czechia to z20; AT/PL/SI/SK/FR/CH to z18-19. No @2x (404).

providers.signupHint: Create a developer account at developer.mapy.com and generate an API key in the dashboard. The free tier has a monthly request allowance and requests beyond it are billed, so check what is left before a large download. Attribution, including the Mapy.com logo, is required.
providers.quotaNote: Free tier: a monthly request allowance. The terms place no restriction on what the data is used for.

providers.signupHint: Sign up at thunderforest.com and the API key appears on your account dashboard. The free plan covers a limited number of tiles per month.

themes.note: Always JPEG whatever extension the URL asks for - Mapbox says so explicitly.

providers.signupHint: Create an account at mapbox.com and copy the default public token, or make a new one, from Account → Tokens. Tiles are billed after a free monthly allowance, so watch the usage page before a large download.

themes.note: Stops at zoom 16, which caps how large it can be printed.

providers.attribution: © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors
providers.signupHint: Sign up at client.stadiamaps.com for the free developer plan and create a property to get an API key. The EU endpoint is used here. Stamen Watercolor stops at zoom 16.
providers.quotaNote: The key goes in an Authorization header as 'Stadia-Auth <key>', which keeps it out of logs.

providers.signupHint: Sign up free at geoapify.com and copy the API key from your project. The free plan gives 3 000 credits a day and a tile costs a quarter of a credit – about 12 000 tiles daily.

providers.signupHint: No account needed – these tiles come from the OpenStreetMap Foundation's donated servers. Their usage policy does not allow bulk downloading, so WTF will not mass-download from here. Use it to find your area, then pick a provider with an API key to download it.

providers.signupHint: No account needed. Community-run on donated capacity, so bulk downloading is disabled. Contours and relief shading make it one of the better-looking maps at wall size.

providers.signupHint: No key needed on this legacy endpoint, but Esri has been moving open access to a token-based one and the terms are the least clear of any provider here. Downloading in bulk is disabled until somebody has read them.
providers.quotaNote: Viewing only until the terms have been read. See docs/design/providers.md §3.
